reviewText:
My impressions of Fatherree's book:

Pros --

-- The photos are almost without exception beautiful and help to explain and illustrate points the author is trying to make.

-- Chapter 6 ("Tridacnid troubles) sets out a good amount of information on diseases that I have never seen in any other place.

-- The third chapter, on identification of the various species, is very useful, clear and well done overall.  The photos in this chapter are invaluable and beautiful.

Cons --

-- The "conversational style" is something a reader may like, or may not. I did not.  I want a clear explanation of a topic, not a conversation with someone who is trying to be casual, witty and amusing for reasons that don't help the explanation along.  The author is apparently trying, in part, to make the book entertaining enough so that the reader wants to learn about the subject; virtually anyone who buys this book, though, already has enough interest in the subject to sustain them through the reading of the book.

-- The text on pages 130 and 131 is juxtaposed one with the other.

-- The chapter that many readers would want to be the most complete and cutting-edge (that on care of clams in the aquarium, Chapter 5) is the least informational of the book.  The worst section in that chapter is probably the section on lighting.  This section includes absolutely no mention of lighting intensity in any usably objective terms (PAR or even lux), and wastes five paragraphs with a repetitive monologue of his subjective opinions on the 'looks' of various color temperature bulbs.  This chapter also includes a section on feeding, which spends ALL of its ten pages explaining how, how much, what and when to feed, only to conclude with the recommendation "if you want to avoid all of this, just do what I've done for years (as have a gazillion other hobbyists) and only keep tridacnids in well-established, well-stocked aquariums with bright lights and don't worry about them.(p. 183)"  It should also be pointed out that the book devotes most of Chapter 2 to why Tridacnids need not be fed at all!  Lastly, there was no information in the chapter on care of clams that is not currently what passes for common knowledge in the hobby.  While this is fine, in the sense that a book can be usefully a compilation of common practices, I expected more.

In summary: a book that most interested hobbyists will find is worth owning, in spite of the fact that it falls short of a bar that has been set by recent books in the hobby, including Wilkerson's "Clownfishes", Borneman's "Aquarium Corals" and the three volumes of Delbeek and Sprung's "The Reef Aquarium".
summary: Good, but a bit overrated by other reviewers

But in the meantime, I didn't want to do nothing.  The odor was alienating him from the family and I was very concerned about the health implications of having all that bacteria in his mouth.

I went ahead and bought this product.  I'm so glad I did! We've been adding the liquid to his water bowl as the label instructs for about a week and a half. He's a "snuggler" so now that his breath isn't so awful and people aren't wanted to push him away, he's really bonding with the family. I'm not sure I would have even believed someone if they would have told me this were possible in such a short time without a professional cleaning and without a brushing regimine.  Now, to be fair, this poor pup does have advanced periodontial problems with alot of calculus scaling (hard brown build up) on his teeth and he will need additional help.  I really don't anticipate Suzie's will miraculously make the hard build-up disappear (but hey, I'd be thrilled if it did).  But just to eliminate the infection and odor is going to go a long way towards improving this little guy's oral health and will make it possible for us to get him additional help after he is nursed back to health.

Our other family dog is still quite young and has no tartar or staining on her teeth; I'm eager to see if this acts as a preventative so she won't even develop these issues. I'm very hopeful based on the dramatic decrease in bad odor that it is at the very least improving her oral health.  I really wouldn't be suprised if it delivers in this regard.

Bottom line: some advanced doggie dental issues can't be fixed with Suzie's Tartar Liquid, but in our family, the dramatic results in eliminated bad odor have far exceeded our expectations in a very short time. reviewText: I was betrayed by a dog "expert" that swears by these that they're the greatest thing ever.  I suspect Planet Dog has in fact betrayed them by letting their quality control slip.  The green parts are glued on, but not very well.  I don't leave any toys with my dog unsupervised but my puppy ripped Australia off and swallowed it in only a minute of play.  Several of the other continents are peeling off and hanging my a thread.  I felt like returning the ball with the green piece, poop and all.

Like other Planet Dog toys, this ball is good, but not the best.  The knot in the rope comes undone quickly, so you will have to tie it again.  Also, if you have a constant chewer/mouther on balls (and don't just use it for fetching), the outer shell of the ball can come apart off of the inner shell that has the continents on it.  But that is usually after lots and lots of chewing.  Other than that, my dogs LOVE these balls.  They love the softness and the chewability.

The Orbee ball material is great -- very flexible (so better for a dog's teeth) but also very durable and virtually indestructible (except the world portion can eventually peel back/off the ball, but that's not a big deal because the ball itself stays in tact) . . . like the versions with the rope, because I can throw the ball a farther distance with it.

I got an orbee for a gift for my bulldog a few years back and it lasted about four years of off and on chewing.  We have proceeded to give planet dog products to all friends with dogs, especially ones with a proclivity to chew up supposed "indestructible" toys over the past few years.

However, since getting the new versions of the same toys, the dog has chewed right through them within weeks, sometimes within a day.  Either the bulldog has gotten even stronger jaws during his fifth and sixth years of life or the orbee's have declined in quality.  Based on the information I have on hand, I am going to lean towards the latter.

I am pretty disappointed because I finally thought I found a dog toy brand that would last more than a week or two.

This is a great toy and company for most normal dogs, but stay away from it for super-strong chewers.
summary: Don't last as long as they used to...

As a side note - I overheard my vet telling a client that the flea bombs are worthless and not to use them as they do not actually get into the cracks and crevices where fleas and their eggs hide.

One other note is to remember to wash all your bedding and vacuum everywhere (especially your furniture and under beds and furniture with open bottoms) in your house if you have a flea infestation.  Seeing a couple fleas on your animals may or may not warrant that. Also remember to empty your vacuum cleaner right away after vacuuming and dispose of the bag or contents in a bag, seal and put in a garbage can ASAP so the live fleas do not get back out and reinfest your home.

reviewText:

Methodology:
2 cats
4 litter boxes
1 month with daily scooping.

I'm a two-cat mom and have been a clumping clay litter user for decades. I came a bit late to the natural litter party, because I was afraid natural litters would clump poorly/smell bad etc. Swheat Scoop is the second natural litter I've tried, and I had planned to try them all but this stuff is so great that I've decided there's no need to look further.

There is no such thing as a cat litter that never smells bad, has no dust, never tracks at all, and produces clumps so perfect that they neither stick to the side/bottom of the box nor crumble apart a bit. That said, Swheat Scoop is the closest to perfect I've ever found, in ALL of these respects.

Smell: Slightly "barnyard"-like (it is wheat, after all), but I only notice it when I'm scooping out the box; if you scoop daily, you will not have an ambient smell. (We live in a 1-BR condo and the litter box is in the bathroom, so I would notice if there was a lingering smell.)

Dust: Hands down, the least dusty litter (clay or natural) I've ever tried.

Tracking: Minimal, on par with the lowest-tracking clay litters I've used, and superior to the lightweight (pine/cedar) natural litters. Swheat Scoop's consistency is quite like Grape Nuts cereal (sorry to gross out anyone who eats Grape Nuts), so because the granules are on the heavier side they tend not to track.

Clumps: Not perfectly tight, but they can be scooped easily enough. With a high volume of urine, the clumps do stick to the bottom/sides a bit, but in my experience the tighter-clumping clay litters adhere MUCH more to the bottom and sides. (One of our cats pees a ton and the side-sticking drove me nuts with clay litter.) And as another reviewer mentioned, keeping the litter level high enough definitely mitigates this problem.

I haven't experienced the bug problem others mentioned, but I'm willing to risk it considering how great this stuff is.
summary: Better than other natural litters AND clay litters.

reviewText: We've used Swheat for at least 10 years, and have never had a 'bug' problem with it. We've lived in the east and now in the desert southwest, and no problems in either climate.  There has been virtually no smell - even when we come back from vacations and the clumping action is remarkable.  We've also disposed of the clumps in the toilet and have never had a plumbing problem.  If it sticks to the bottom of the litter pan, chances are you don't have enough in the pan. We use a pan with a sifter insert (same pan for 10 years too!)and they seem to be made for each-other.

I tried and tried to like this product, as I despise the clay based toxicity of most kitty litters, but there is one "con" that outweighs every "pro": BUGS. The first time I noticed what I believe are called wheat weevils, I threw away the litter in the pans and the fresh litter sealed in an airtight container, and cleaned EVERYTHING. I purchased new Swheat Scoop and, weeks later, past what should have been the next egg hatching cycle, I found what looked like millions of the bugs in a fresh box. They clearly are Trojan Horsing themselves into my life via the factory. I CANNOT get rid of them. I am having to have an exterminator come to my house and the company says I have to throw away all the grains in my home on top of it all. I have switched to a non-food based litter. I know that the invasion of these bugs is wholly due to chance, but I would like to warn those considering the purchase of Swheat Scoop: there IS a chance these bugs will move in and they  will do everything in their power to stay.

I've been using Swheat Scoop for years - switched from World's Best(which, alas, had too much dust for me.  Swheat Scoop is fine with the cats and doesn't get tracked around as much as some other brands.

There is a problem with food moth and other bug infestations in our now hotter summers. Cure: crumple up a few bay leaves in the open litter tray and pop a few in the bag of unused litter.  This also works to protect your herbs, dried beans, grains, etc.

Because this litter is a wheat product, it attracts meal bugs. My bag actually came with the bugs in it - when I opened the bag, left it in the bathroom, and came back a few hours later, the bugs were crawling out of the bag and up the wall. I have done everything to eliminate the bugs. Naturally I disposed of every crumb of Swheat Scoop. But once you have these in your house, it is very difficult to get rid of them permanently, due to the life cycle of meal bugs. You think you've eliminated them, and then a few months later, they're back. Do not buy this product, even if you think it works great as a cat litter. You run the risk of being plagued by bugs forever.

I just switched to this brand about 2 weeks ago.

Pros: Light smell, really does smell like wheat.  Inexpensive and can be found at Target, etc.  Two cats adapted to the new litter within hours.  Healthy for cats.

Cons: I've found that it does not clump well for pee!  Urine often is clumped to the bottom and sides of the box.

I had a chance recently to test out my Petmate Fresh Flow fountain against the "original" Drinkwell pet fountain.
Style: The Drinkwell has a small waterfall which comes out a chute at the top, drops through air, and hits a sloped ramp in the dish. The ramp reduces the splash and noise you would get from a stream hitting the water in the dish directly. In contrast, the Petmate model dribbles the stream of water entirely down a sloped ramp that runs from the top of the unit down into the dish.
Noise: I filled them both up and placed them side by side. My cats were immediately attracted to the Drinkwell. Which makes sense, because it's noiser than the Fresh Flow. Despite the ramp, there are gentle splashing noises. More importantly, the relatively soft hum of the pump is MUCH louder. (If you like ambient splashing sounds, get a CD.) The Fresh Flow wasn't totally quiet, and the pump buzzes when it's warming up and when it's low on water, but overall it's the quieter of the two.
Maintenance: I found the Fresh Flow much less complicated to put together, to move around, and to clean. The first time I filled up the Drinkwell and added the reservoir to the back, I spilled a lot of water. So I ended up putting the whole thing onto a large tray, to reduce the mopping for next time. My cats like to step in their dishes, so periodic cleaning is a must for both units. (In case you're wondering: When the water in the dish gets too cruddy, they drink from the flowing water at the top.) The Fresh Flow is sturdier--it's a lot easier to pick it up and move it to the kitchen sink. Without using the tray underneath the Drinkwell, I suspect I'd drop parts and spill dirty water fairly often. [Side note: What I would *really* like for either model, is some kind of liner for the dish that I could lift out, rinse, throw in the dishwasher, and then put back.]
Capacity: The Drinkwell has several size models and varying capacities for reservoirs. The Fresh Flow's strength is its weakness: The sturdy structure and tight-fitting parts mean you can't just swap out the reservoir for a bigger one... you have to buy a larger unit. This is why I recommend their largest one.
Cat Preference: In spite of their initial attraction to the Drinkwell, water levels in both units after a few days suggested that my cats were equally likely to drink from either fountain.
Summary: Kudos to the Petmate R&D for improving on the "original" pet fountain. (Disclaimer: I have no affiliation with Petmate, except as a satisfied customer.)
One other note... One of the big reasons to get a water fountain for your pet is to improve their health by encouraging them to drink more. For cat owners, if you do this, you might soon be looking at automatic litterboxes. If so, you might consider the Petmate Purrforma unit, an improvement over the "original" LitterMaid.

There are a number of similar products on the market, and I've had varied results with them. In pet stores, the ubiquitous choice is Nature's Miracle Stain & Odor Remover for Pets. It's guaranteed to work or your money back. My multiple experiences with it made me wish I took them up on their offer. The company makes an effective laundry booster, but their stain and odor eliminator never quite did the job. Plus, odors came back over the following days. A better product I found was OUT! Pet Stain and Odor Remover, 32 Ounce. I'm mentioning it primarily to give an idea of how it compares to the others. It does a credible job, and I found it much more effective than Nature's Miracle. It did not get rid of odors completely, but with multiple applications, it did a workable job. Odors did come back over the following days, requiring additional applications. The Lambert Kay works best among these brands. It does a very good job up front. While it might not eliminate every odor on the first application, it's the most likely choice to do so. Faint remnants of odors after an initial application might not be there two days later, while the opposite is true with competing products. I consider this product the hands down winner. reviewText: This is a wonderful all natural product to help clean you dog's eyes.  I've had poodles and cockers all my life and this product does the trick.

My cat tends to get goopy, encrusted eyes as a symptom of feline herpes. He graciously suffered my attempts to clean his eyes with clean hands and a damp tissue, but I knew there had to be a better way. Eyes So Bright by Ark Naturals was the solution. The herbs in this product are the same one would use for human health, and have similar uses. Even so, there are a few small issues that caused me to drop one star.

My first attempts to use this product failed miserably. My cat was very sensitive to the astringent quality of the fluid, and it took a while for him to adjust to the sensation. Further complicating things is the design of the bottle. The plastic bottle is a little hard to squeeze, and the push-top cap (like a shampoo bottle) just makes it harder to be sure of the amount of fluid I'm squeezing out. I tried to follow the instructions on the bottle to simply saturate a cotton ball, hold it to the affected eye, and allow the product to seep out into the eye. That didn't work as my cat was too jumpy and the liquid went everywhere but into the eye. Then I tried squeezing a little fluid from the cotton ball into the eye--better, but the astringency was difficult for him to bear.

Now I've switched to using a circular cotton pad (like a make-up pad) cut into fourths, and with a saturated pad, I dab gently at the eye and clear debris that way. Now that my cat is more accustomed to the fluid, he seems to welcome the cooling relief and now I can hold the pad to his eye, squeeze in a little fluid, or wipe his eyelid, and he responds well to all of these. He still gets encrusted and goopy eyes, but now I can clean them with ease.

Ingredients (as listed on the bottle):
De-ionized water, traditional hand filet aloe juice HF, FG, witch hazel, goldenseal fluid extract, gotu kola fluid extract, echinacea fluid extract.

If you have a pet with weeping or encrusted eyes, try this product. It'll take a little while for everyone to get adjusted, but the benefits are well worth it.

Cedarific is the BEST cat litter I have ever used.  I have four cats and two of them only use this brand.  It's easy to clean the box and it smells great.  I am so glad to find it on Amazon...I did purchase it at a local grocery store and it was discontinued....thanks for stocking this amazing product....you have made me and my cats HAPPY CATS.

reviewText: I bought these for my mom's cats. Most of them just ignored the fresheners, but one cat was crazy for them! He'd rub his head all over the tin and try to bite it open. I really know if it freshened his breath, though.

You should probably hide these somewhere OUTSIDE your house if you want to get any sleep at night.  My cats have been known to wake me up rummaging through drawers looking for them.  Rattle the tin and be prepared to be run down!  I've never seen my kids more excited about treats.  Greenies get left on open on the table & never touched, but these have to be locked up.  Not the best smelling, but they love them.

If you buy one tin, buy ten because your cat will think these are wildly delicious. Strangely enough they are shaped like fish, but they contain ingredients like green tea extract and rosemary oil.

We went through one tin in a week and my cats thought these were the best treats they had ever tasted.

I had no idea cats would enjoy rosemary oil in a cat treat, nor did I think they would paw at the empty tin begging for me to buy more. Definitely a treat to hide in a safe place.

Even after taking these out of the packaging and box, my cats were clawing at the box to get more. You have to hide the box

in a high place or in a drawer or they will find a way to get into the container.

I'm not sure who enjoys these treats more. I love

seeing how much my two cats enjoy these treats. The

tin with two treats can also work as a training tool

because the cats will instantly respond when they

hear the treats being shaken in the tin.

~The Rebecca Review

While these do absolutely nothing as far as improving my cats' breath, both of them go nuts over these.  They bat the tin around as a toy, and when I pull one out to give it to them, I can get both of them to stand on their hind legs begging for the treats.  This ALMOST goes over bigger than catnip in our household!!  Almost.  :o)

One year, we bought my cat a tin of these. Her breath always smells like the other fish treats we give her, so the idea of 'breath fresheners' sounded amusing.

My cat went crazy over these. We set the tin on a table, and she instantly jumped up and started attacking them.

Be warned though, the treats have a very strong smell of liver. They really don't do anything for the cat's breath, but the cat's love them, and that's what really matters.
My cat loves these. Recognizes the little tin box, and will meow like crazy until I open it to give him some.

My cat is very picky, but when I brought these & Greenies home, she tore into them. When I put away the tin, she opened the cabinet and ransacked everything inside. She ended up hitting the switch to turn off our dishwasher and I had to meet with a service repairman to figure out why the dishwasher would no longer run.

reviewText: While they don't improve her breath, my cat loves these treats and will go to great lengths to search for them.

reviewText: Being limited on storage space in our nursery, we purchased this closet organizer.  We love it.  It has really helped our storage problems.  The organizer itself seems very well built and sturdy.  The shelves will hold quite a bit of stuff, for lack of a better term.  We really are satisfied with this product. ***Update - after ten months the shelves are starting to sag and bow, nothing that will hinder it's use but doesn't look as pretty as it did!

I've had this exact organizer made by Kolcraft in blue for nearly 2 years. I love it! My two sons share a room and closet, this allows me to keep all their clothes in the closet rather than use a dresser. I will probably buy another one when baby #3 arrives in February.

reviewText: A friend of mine who's hamsters passed away gave me this CritterTrail One cage because I got a new dwarf hamster. I don't know if it's from age, but the wheel makes a racket! My tiny little hamster woke me up at 4:00 am with the wheel 3 nights in a row! What i do now is wedge toilet paper rolls into the wheel so my hamster can't get in it at night, and I take them out in the morning. This has been working, but the loss of exersise may be bad for the hamster. I would advise purchasing a new snap on wheel that doesn't make all that noise. The cage, however, has a great design and Hamlet (my hamster) seems to love it. The water bottle does leak, and my dwarf hamster had trouble reaching it, so I bought a new one for about $2 and it works fine. The cage is easy to clean and my hamster loves it, escpecially since he's a dwarf, so there's a lot of room. It has its disadvantages, but all in all, it's a good cage for the price.

reviewText: I bought this cage for my daughters 2 mice.  The mice seem to love it but I think it was a mistake to buy this cage.  My husband had to assemble it because the pieces would all fall apart while I was trying to assemble it.  You have to take the cage apart to clean it and then its impossible to assemble again.  My husband has to put it back together after each cleaning.  The water bottle leaks everywhere especially when you pick up the cage to move it from one location to another.  The door is very easy to open and I find the mice pushing on it frequently...they also push on the roof opening and I know they will figure out how to open both doors soon.  Put a lock on the door for extra safety.  I recommend buying a regular metal cage. I would never put a hamster in this cage they would open it for sure.

We bought this cage when we got our hamster.  The latch to hold the door shut is terrible.  While camping for two days, our cats got the cage open and killed the hamster.  It was not fun explaining to our three year old son that the cats got into the cage and killed the hamster.  If I ever buy a new hamster and cage I will definately NOT get this same cage again.  Plus, another negative is that the wheel made way too much noise when the hamster would run on it.

I bought this a few weeks ago and i had to replace the water bottle because it was leaking annd i had to buy a new wheel because the racket it made drove me crazy! It kind of small but luckily you can add attachments! So all in all its ok but i wouldnt recommend it very highly.

I have researched a number of used ones on various auction sites, many with the same broken clip.  Super Pet, the one's who build it (can be found on net) will be happy to sell you another one for $2 with $6 shipping.  We decided to by a new one because of the high cost to replace only the lid.  We are now the proud owners of 2 CritterTrail One cages that have a broken lid.  My suggestion is to find a better built product.

My cats have pushed this all around my room trying to get the cage open WITHOUT SUCCESS! (Unlike with the Space Station Habitrail. RIP Spunky and Snowflake) Locks great. Cleaning hasn't proposed a problem for me as it has others. I've figured out a way to get the top off without it coming apart.

She loves the top tray, where she's made her nest and spends most of her days.  She only comes down when its time to eat or run in her wheel. reviewText: My daughter held two gerbils in this cage. They chewed through the top lid and actually made a 1 inch hole in it. we have to recover this hole with tape everyday and but a rock on top so that it will stay shut. I have years of experience with all sorts of animals that require all sorts of cages and I have never had a cage so badly made before.

Gerbils like to dig, so all the bedding came flying out of the cage.  And they chewed on all the plastic joints inside the cage.  Since then, I've bought an aquarium for them which has turned out to be a whole lot better.  I still have this cage, held together with masking tape, and let my gerbils play in it while I clean the aquarium.  I think that the Critter Trail One is more suited for hamsters and mice.

It is a great toy and my cats greatly enjoyed it. After they got tired to play with it they used it as an automatic petting machine :) Check out a  video I took: [...]

Unfortunately, the toy broke rather quickly. I took it apart and the mechanism had quite flimsy and weak gear wheels made of very soft plastic...

I wish they made the thing more reliable but other than that is it a fun toy for cats.

My cats LOVE this toy. It's one of their 3 favorite toys of all time. (Their other favorite toys are a cat-n-mouse toy and a scratching post where a battery-powered toy goes round when they scratch, followed by the "fishing pole" types of toys.) My playful cats love Panic Mouse (of course) but my less-coordinated, less playful cats love it too.

When I bought this toy I was sceptical about whether my cats would play with it. (They often play with a new toy for maybe 15 minutes a few times and then they're bored with the toy for at least several months.) And Panic Mouse was fairly expensive so I hated to spend that much money on a toy that wouldn't get much use. But since I rescue and foster cats, I thought some might like it and hoped it would be worthwhile overall.

When I got it home, three of my cats immediately began watching it. Soon they were sitting in a circle around it playing. Later, when I made it slower, the cats who play less often (who had been watching it without playing) began playing too. I turn it off when the cats leave the area but they come back every half hour or so to play again. I originally had it in my living room. After my cats left the area, I moved it to my bedroom so a different group of cats could try it. But when the "living room cats" came back, they were upset that the toy wasn't there anymore so I had to move it back to the living room.

I like how you can adjust the speed and angle of the toy. Some of my cats like it slow, others medium or fast. Some of my cats like the toy to be dragged along the ground, others like it in the air. This toy allows you to give your cat what it wants in terms of slow/fast or air/ground play. And unlike humans, it can and will play for hours at a time.

All my cats love this toy. It's the first cat toy that all my cats have enjoyed. I don't know how long it will last but if it lasts a whole month, it will have been well worth the price because I've had it two days and it has already entertained my cats for about 30 hours. They've played more hours with Panic Mouse in two days than they have with most of their toys, even the toys we've had for over a year.

my cat likes this toy a lot.  she gets very excited to play with it.  i think the toy is not well made - my cat frequently topples the toy even with the extra stabilizer that comes with the toy.  the wand is also ripped off quite easily.  if your cat is very gentle, this is the toy for it.  otherwise, no.
summary: 3 stars, but only because my cat likes the toy

reviewText: This is the ONLY toy my 8-year old cat plays with for more than 3 minutes at a time...and often more than once a day. He actually "asks" for it to be turned on! Sometimes he plays with it for so long he exhausts himself and ends up lying on his back just trying to hit it with one paw 'cause he's too tired to do much else. It's an amazing cat toy, unlike anything else on the market. Go for it!

My cat received this toy as a gift from his grandmother last christmas!  It was his favorite toy!  Toy ran very well for the first two months and then the motor started going.  Replacement of batteries didn't work. Finally because he would always sit by the toy wanting to play - I decided to take it apart and see what the problem was.  The electrical wires came apart.  I fixed it and he resumed play.  This was good for about a week before it broke again.  I have thus repaired it 5 times but now it is finally irrepairable.  The company won't take it back, fix it or exchange it as it only had a 30 day warranty.  He really loves this toy and even though it is broken continues to sit near it and try to play with it.  Becuase he loves it so much I was considering buying him a new one.  But sad to say the toy doesn't seem to be made well and it isn't exactly cheap by way of cat toys.  So I am reluctant. But like I said before it was his favorite and entertained him for long periods of time. Too bad it isn't made well. Hope this helps.

My cat thinks this is the best toy he's ever seen.  However, apart from the problem with the cat easily knocking it over, the toy began to develop problems within the first month.

First the motor began to act strange, and wouldn't fully twirl around, getting stuck at points (different batteries didn't fix it).  Also, our cat has learned how to break the string, requiring a never ending supply of new strings.

Without these problems this would be a great toy.  With them, I'd be reluctant to recommend it to anyone one.  Broken strings are common with cat toys, but the problem with the motor has made it unusable.  I may have just been unlucky, but this was my experience with it, and I'm not willing to spend more to find out.

wow.. to "mom4three" reviewer.  I was just looking around to see a review on the product, but you purchased ALL of the products made by the Panic Mouse company, and NONE OF THEM work? O_O.  It's kind of hard to belive...

reviewText: My cats love this toy!  It is very well made and stable.  I haven't had to purchase the extra wand and mouse yet but am glad they are available just incase.
summary: Excellent Toy and a great price!

reviewText: My cats absolutely LOVE this toy! They even play with it when it isn't turned on. Well worth the money. I do suggest if your cats are hard on toys to get a few of the replacment wands to go with it.

Ok..we bought a "Panic Mouse" for our cats/kittens. While the older cats walked by it with expressions of indifference. The kittens have a blast with it!

It moves and turns randomly so they never know which way it will go..ok..I admit..once in awhile one gets knocked in the head by it...but it's still funny! You can adjust the speed so it goes slower, which we did until they got the hang of it then it was FULL power. It even keeps the kids entertained! Just remember to shut if off or you will be buying batteries left and right.

If you buy one buy the extra wand and 3 mice, as the strings are pretty flimsy and break easy. Or go buy some string and a few pom poms and make them yourself.

Although the toy is great and our cat likes it very much, it's extremely fragile. After a few times the "motor" is not running properly any more. I've ordered a second one since I thought the problem was caused by coincidence, but the second one gave the same problems after 3 times use. All in all too expensive for the quality offered !

Even with the stablizing bar in place my Siamese overpowered the Panic Mouse within 10 minutes and sent it tumbling down a flight of stairs, bending the arm, impacting it's functionality (now limited).  The thing sucks batteries four times as fast as the last moving toy I purchased.  Medioce at best; poor if you have an "assertive" feline when it comes to hunting.

I left my cat playing with the 'mouse' while I left the room, and when I returned in a few minutes he had the cord wrapped around his neck and the more he pulled, the tighter it became.  I feel I can never let him play with this unsupervised.

Panic Mouse Original I recieved the panic mouse as a gift, and it has been better than I could've anticipated. I have a houseful of cats, all sizes and personalities, and it was fascinating to watch all of the differing games and strategies they would devise. Some would try to grab the fur ball and sit on it, some would lay down and bat at it; some would keep their distance and watch intently. I've been amazed how it has continued to work, in spite of much feline abuse. They pull the mouse over, drag the fur ball across the room, and yet, it keeps on working. It has lasted longer than any other toy I've bought for them, and they remain fascinated by it. I recommend this mouse highly!
This is a replacement. It is great the cat loves it and he is 18 years old.

I have 5 cats, Sandy (16-17), Stinkey (11), Tiger (2), Panda and Mylo (8 months).  We origionally bought the Panic mouse for Tiger when we went to get pictures with santa for the humane society.  My mom was reluctant at first (she didn't want to spend $30 on it) But it was the best investment ever! Tiger loved it!
Sandy isn't into the fast movement (she falls over) but she sits and watches. Stinkey is the queen, so when she's playing the kittens all stay back! haha it's an amazing toy!
In September Panda and Mylo were dumped in a ditch, so we took them in and it's their favorite toy!
I added a bell to the wand and it made it even more popular!
As soon as they hear the bell, the kittens come running!

We've had the panic mouse for a year and 4 months.  The origional wand finally broke this morning! (Mylo likes to chew strings)
I would recommend this toy to anyone who has or is thinking about getting kitties!

My cat loves this toy....she plays with it all the time...only thing she doesn't like it turned on....she won't play with it then. But as long as it is off she will play with it for hours on end! Another cat of the family likes it too, but he won't play with it very often....and then the other cat hates it.

I have had cats all my life and bought hundreds of toys for cats and this Panic Mouse is the greatest toy.  My cat loves it.  Whoever made this toy has really done their research.  Every other toy I have had like this just goes around and round.  This one goes every which way and changes directions, which cats need and love.  They do not get bored.  My cat will play with this for hours, and I mean hours on end.  She is an indoor cat, so she needs the exercise and she is happier than I have ever seen her since we got this toy.  Anyone who has a cat should have this toy.  I suggest buying re-chargeable batteries, b/c your cat won't let you turn it off.
summary: The Greatest Cat Toy Ever Made

reviewText: I purchased the Panic mouse to entertain my five cats who love to play.. I work out of my home a couple days a week and when I am home my cats assume I am there to play with them which makes it hard for me to do my job..problem solved , I turn the Panic mouse on and they are entertained for hours at a time...Surprising enough all five love it and  is a  real hoot to watch them interact  with it.. Now that is keeping me from my work..ha hah. Panic Mouse is  a very clever  toy and well made .. I would Highly recommend for any cat owner.

My cats went bonkers over the Panic Mouse when I first turned it on, but they quickly developed a tolerance to it. One cat now lies on the floor in front of it and passively whaps it when the mouse wand moves past him. Another cat sits still and allows the wand to "pet" him. Yes, the Vortex D-1 and its accessories are a bit of a pain to use. It is really a specialty filter, not something for the average consumer to use on a regular basis. But if you have an aquarium with water that looks like pea soup, or suspect a water-born parasite is loose in your tank, this is the filter to have and it is worth the extra effort it takes to use it. It can clear a completely opaque green tank to crystal clear in less than an hour. The diatomaceous earth filter will also filter out water-borne nasty critters that are too small to see with the naked eye. You end up with a tank with completely polished water.

In my case, I have a very large tank. When cleaning time comes along, I invariably leave a mess suspended in the water from the stirred-up gravel or from algae cleaned from the glass. If I put a Vortex into the tank before I clean - voila! - no crud suspended in the water, just crystal clear beauty.

So yes, it is messy to set up, noisy, messy to clean - and it does exactly what is designed to do: Clean the worst messy excuse for aquarium water in a short amount of time into a crystal clear paradise for your fish. 'Nuff said!
summary: It does what it is designed to do...

Having been keeping fish for over 40 years I can honestly say when it comes to polishing your aquarium water to an almost surreal clarity nothing - absolutely nothing comes close to the Diatom by Vortex.

These amazing filters remove particulate matter down to one micron in size - they're the only filter on the planet that can rid a tank of parasites like Ich without the use of harsh mediations (you'll need to run it for 48-73 hours to catch the life stage when the parasite is free swimming)

I use the D1 for smaller tanks up to a 50 gallon and my XL for tanks 55 gallons and above. These patented filter bags are amazing but they do break down and cake up with DE (diatomaceous earth) so it's critical to have replacement filter bags on hand.

I replace the bags about every three months but the, I use both Diatoms frequently, at least one a week. So depending upon how often you use yours your mileage will of course vary.

One trick with the D1 bag I recommend is to cut off the yellow pull strap. It makes it so much easier to insert the bag and turbulence tube and pulling of the filter bag for cleaning or replacement is still a breeze - just make sure you pull from the black plastic connector of the bag and not the bag itself.

ALLPET is hands down one my favorite and most trusted of Amazon sellers. I shop with them frequently, great prices, fast delivery and they're always willing to answer questions or make suggestions.

Replacement parts for both the D1 an XL are becoming harder to find, if you depend on your Diatom as much as I do it makes sense to stock up on filter bags. Also by rotating the bags you can increase their life span dramatically.
